sections.html:
The Jones County Register of Deeds is at 101 Market Street in Trenton. The mailing address is PO Box 189, Trenton, NC 28585, and the phone is 252-448-2551. Monday through Thursday the counter is staffed from morning into late afternoon, and recording stops at 4:30. Fridays are short: open from 8 a.m. to noon, with an 11:30 cutoff for recording.

That short Friday matters for a closing. A deed that reaches the counter after 11:30 on a Friday sits until Monday, so sellers here usually schedule signing early in the week.

Besides land transactions, the office keeps births, deaths, marriages, service discharges, notaries, assumed names and maps. Its land indexes go back to the late 1700s, and records from before 1978 are searched through their own page on the county site.

A deed is $26.00 through page 15, with $4.00 for each later sheet. A deed of trust has a longer base: $64.00 through page 35.

Jones County real estate recording charges
What you are recording or requestingAmount
Loan security (deed of trust)$64.00 to page 35, $4.00 per page past that
Deeds and other instruments$26.00 to page 15, $4.00 per page past that
Combined instruments in one filing$10.00
Release of a deed of trust by satisfactionFree of charge
Document out of format$25.00
Plat sheet$21.00 each
Certified real estate copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 each page after
Plain copy25 cents

The excise stamp is $2.00 for each $1,000 of purchase price, or $1.00 per $500 of consideration. The seller pays it at the counter.

Every deed, together with a completed Tax Certification Form, goes to the Tax Office for approval before the register can record it. The form is also called the Tax Data Sheet or Tax Collection Form, and the register's site links to it.

Two more local rules apply:

  • A county ordinance requires the tax parcel ID number on the first page of every deed.
  • A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for real property that is subject to delinquent taxes.

In practice an unpaid Jones County tax bill can stop a deed at the counter. A seller with back taxes should pay them at or before closing, and the closing agent can settle the bill so the deed is accepted the same day.

Anything on paper filed after July 1, 2002 has to follow the layout rules of G.S. 161-14(b), and the register posts them online. A document that misses the mark is charged $25.00 extra, added to the normal recording fee.

  • Paper size of 8 1/2 by 11 or by 14.
  • A blank 3 inch band at the top of page one, half an inch of margin on its other edges, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Black or dark ink on white stock, type no smaller than 10 points.
  • Text on a single side of each sheet.
  • The instrument type printed right under the top margin, with the preparer identified on page one.

Small print under 10 point that still scans clearly may get the nonstandard fee waived. Maps and plats follow separate rules: they must be 18 by 24 inches, with one mylar and one paper copy, and a Jones County review officer approves the map before it is recorded.

An old mortgage is cleared by recording a satisfaction, and Jones County charges nothing for it. There are two kinds: a Satisfaction of Security Instrument signed by the secured creditor, and a Trustee's Satisfaction signed by a trustee or substitute trustee.

Wills are not recorded at the register. They go to the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, which matters if you are selling an inherited house and do not want to visit the wrong counter.

Under state law a tax lien reaches the parcel on its January 1 listing date, carrying penalties, interest and costs. If it stays unpaid, the county enforces it by filing a foreclosure action in court. Before you sign a sales contract, ask the Jones County tax office for a current payoff figure.

The bill is due September 1. On January 6 it becomes delinquent and 2 percent interest applies for January, followed by 3/4 percent every month. A mailed payment counts by its U.S. Postal postmark, and a postage meter date is not accepted.

The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2022, and the next is set for January 1, 2030. Market changes between those dates are not counted. If you disagree with an assessment, call 252-448-2546 to set up an informal appeal before March 1. Later appeals may need a formal hearing before the county review board.

Visit the tax office at 418 Hwy 58 N in Trenton. The counter shuts at five o'clock Monday through Thursday and at midday on Friday. Partial payments are taken at the Tax Collections Office, and a payment plan is available only if no enforced collection action has begun. Agricultural and forest tracts can qualify for use value taxation, with a new application going to the assessor during the regular January listing period.

Jones County is thinly settled, with 9,575 people and 4,804 housing units spread over 471.37 square miles. A typical owned home is worth $130,300, and owners occupy 79.4 percent of homes. Residents 65 and older are 26.8 percent of the county, so many sales involve an older owner or an estate. Only 46 building permits were issued in 2025, which means a seller mostly competes with other resales, and a house that needs repairs can sit for a long time.

sections.h2: Does a cash sale change the recording steps?
sections.html:
A cash buyer's deed follows the same path as any other. It is approved by the tax office, shows the parcel number on page one, has its stamp paid by the seller, and gets to the register before the weekday or Friday cutoff.

The difference is pace and condition. A cash deal skips the lender appraisal, and the house is bought in its current state. That can help an owner who has liens, a vacant house, tenants or an estate to wind up. Overdue taxes must still be cleared at closing so the register will take the deed.

Before you head to the closing table:

  1. Get the Tax Certification Form approved at the tax office.
  2. Confirm the parcel ID number is on page one.
  3. Pay any delinquent taxes so the register will accept the deed.
  4. Arrive before 4:30 on Monday through Thursday, or before 11:30 on Friday.
  5. Bring a payoff letter if an old deed of trust needs a satisfaction recorded.

faqs.q: What are the Jones County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday it opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m., but the last recording is taken at 4:30 p.m. Friday hours run from 8 a.m. to noon, with the last recording at 11:30 a.m. The phone is 252-448-2551.

faqs.q: Can Jones County record a deed if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: No. A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for property subject to delinquent taxes. Pay the bill first, then present the deed.

faqs.q: What must page one of a Jones County deed show?
faqs.a: The tax parcel ID number, as a county ordinance requires, plus the type of instrument and the preparer's name. A 3 inch top margin and 1/2 inch side margins also apply.

faqs.q: Does Jones County bill for recording a loan release?
faqs.a: No. A satisfaction of a deed of trust is free, whether it is the creditor's signed form or the trustee's.

faqs.q: Where are wills recorded in Jones County?
faqs.a: At the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, phone 252-448-6220, not at the Register of Deeds. The register records the deeds that follow.
